title: Choose the visual world for MeTube
question: A fresh hand, with every earlier direction set aside. The roll assigned the Accession Register. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Accession Register
options.lineage: library accession ledgers, catalogue cards and date-due stamps
options.thesis: Every download is entered in the register with its accession number: the queue is the processing tray, the history is the ledger you search, fetch from and withdraw.
materials: ruled catalogue-card stock with its red header rule
options.viewport: A buckram-green masthead; the URL bar as the accession slip with Download stamped in ink; Downloading as the processing tray, Completed as a ruled register with accession numbers and violet date stamps, each section headed by a brass label holder.
options.risk: Library furniture turns quaint if stamps and brass outweigh the rows; it has to read as a fast ledger first and an archive second.

raised.raise: Every row reads like one end label: the title, then type, format, size and date in fixed monospaced slots, identical down the whole register.
Five states stay unmistakable in one stamp vocabulary: received, in process, waiting, catalogued, withdrawn with its reason.
State prints itself as a dated stamp inside the row, never a badge floating beside it.
The buckram ground carries the chrome at full strength: one flat bookcloth field, never a tint wash.

options.label: Master Control
options.lineage: TV master control rooms, as-run logs and tally lights
options.thesis: MeTube as master control: the queue is the playout schedule, each item's state a tally lamp, the history the as-run log with its timecodes.
options.viewport: A control-room strip with a red ON AIR tally beside each active download and timecode-style speed and ETA; the URL bar as the next-event entry; Completed printed as the as-run log.
options.risk: The closest to where most runs in this category land: a dark control room with red and amber readouts; the light theme has to be the log sheet itself, not an afterthought.

options.label: Crew Terminal
options.thesis: The ship's paperwork made screen: every download a typed line on curved glass, warnings in amber under striped hazard plates, zones stencilled with equipment codes.
options.viewport: Off-white panel chrome framing a CRT well: the URL bar as the query line with a blinking block cursor, active downloads typed out as readouts, the history as a paged log.
options.case: Wins on audience: self-hosters live in terminals and love this film look. Loses on clarity: typed caps and one-line-at-a-time paging fight a 2,000-row history.
options.risk: Near-black phosphor is a saturated look for this category, and the light theme has only the panel chrome to stand on.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.lineage: sneaker archive walls of stacked boxes
options.thesis: A wall of boxes read by their end labels.
options.viewport: The history as a stacked wall of end labels.
options.case: Loses both axes: self-hosters have no tie to sneaker archives, and hinged lids slow a scan of thousands.
options.kept: One label grid ruling every row, the same slots in the same place.
options.risk: A shop display, not a tool.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Downloads as members of a structure under tension.
options.viewport: A force diagram of the queue.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to the audience, and a strut network is no way to read a list.
options.kept: Slack, balanced, stressed and failed states that can never be confused.

options.label: Midnight Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: One continuous scrolling transcript in P1 green.
options.case: Loses both axes against the Crew Terminal's fuller grammar: a single 80-column field cannot carry long titles, and it has no light theme.
options.kept: System state printed as text in the flow, never as chrome.
options.risk: The near-black neon look this category's generated UIs default to.

options.label: Yé-yé Pop Sleeve
options.thesis: One flat saturated ground, a cropped portrait, four titles in a corner.
options.viewport: A single release on a flooded ground.
options.case: Loses both axes: a closed set of four tracks is the opposite of an open history.
options.kept: Total commitment to one flat ground colour.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: Everything drawn in glyph density on one character grid.
options.viewport: The page as a live character grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: spectacle with no purpose in a download manager.
options.kept: One strict grid governs everything, captions included.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The self-hosted app UI played straight, the way Sonarr, Jellyfin or Immich look, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Neutral surfaces, a blue primary and clean dense tables: the layout you know, refined.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other self-hosted app, by design.
